copy: EVERY CHANGE ENTERS A SYSTEM — A policy edit, model update, data field, or workflow shortcut can alter outcomes far beyond the place it began.
The problem: Consequence Propagation fails when the underlying decision, audience, or evidence boundary is left implicit.
The system: make the mechanism inspectable—show what enters, what changes, who retains authority, and what leaves the system.
Evidence context: W3C PROV Primer: provenance supports error checking, responsibility tracing, process repetition, version relationships, sources and attribution.
Demo: walk through one bounded state change in the Build 029 prototype. Show the interaction or decision path, not an invented result.
Implication: Consequence Propagation can make the relevant structure visible and discussable. It does not by itself prove performance, compliance, safety, effectiveness, causation, or endorsement.
Explore Build 029, Consequence Propagation: watch the cut, inspect the motion argument, test the interactive prototype, and review its evidence boundary.
